subject: MSA / Order Form — SLA: uptime thresholds, emergency patch window, and credit triggers
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@gridpay.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA / Order Form — SLA: uptime thresholds, emergency patch window, and credit triggers

Hi Rafael / Laura,

Thanks for the draft. Our legal team flagged the SLA section — two items in particular: (1) the uptime buckets in Exhibit A look tighter than we expected (the 99.9% baseline would expose us to larger credits for short incidents), and (2) the emergency patch/maintenance window language implies Redwood can schedule hotfixes with short notice, which is a concern for our ops schedule.

Attached are the redlines they returned (redline_msa_sla.pdf) plus a suggested SLO matrix from our reliability team. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a 30-minute notification minimum for emergency patches affecting service availability, and whether we can add a de‑minimis clause that caps credits for events under 5 minutes?

We'd like to keep momentum — Tom (cc'd) is our procurement lead and would like to close this week if possible.

Thanks,
Claire Huang
Head of Ops, GridPay
Attachments: redline_msa_sla.pdf, proposed_slo_matrix.xlsx

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@gridpay.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@gridpay.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — SLA: uptime thresholds, emergency patch window, and credit triggers

Claire — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. I reviewed GridPay's suggestions with legal and product. High level: we're open to moderating the uptime buckets but need to preserve a meaningful availability commitment; the de‑minimis clause (events under 5 minutes) is reasonable if paired with clarifying measurement windows.

Two specific asks from our side:
- Can GridPay accept the adjusted credit cap we propose in section 4.2 (max cumulative credits per rolling 12 months = 25% of monthly fees)?
- For emergency patches that materially reduce functionality, Redwood can implement a short notice hotfix, but we propose a 2‑hour minimum advance notification for non-critical patches and a documented emergency criteria for <2‑hour windows to prevent abuse.

I've attached our suggested compromise redline (redline_msa_sla.pdf — v2) and a short response ladder (rdw_response-ladder.docx) that maps incident severities to response times and contact windows. Kimberly — can you confirm product/ops are aligned with the 2‑hour proposal? Laura / Aditya — legal review appreciated.

Next steps: if GridPay accepts the credit cap and the emergency criteria, we can prepare a DocuSign-ready order form and aim for execution this week.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline_msa_sla.pdf (v2), rdw_response-ladder.docx

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, Claire Huang <claire.huang@gridpay.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — SLA: uptime thresholds, emergency patch window, and credit triggers

Rafael / team — product & SRE reviewed. Short summary of our suggested edits (see attached SLO matrix):
- Keep 99.9% as the Premium tier baseline, but add a rolling 7‑day smoothing window for incident measurement to avoid crediting transient spikes. That addresses GridPay's concern about short incidents causing outsized credits.
- De‑minimis clause: agree to exclude single incidents < 5 minutes unless they contribute to a repeated failure pattern within 24 hours.
- Emergency/hotfix window: we can accept a "30‑minute notification minimum" only for customer‑scheduled maintenance that the customer authorizes; for Redwood‑initiated emergency patches that resolve a P1 security vulnerability, we need the ability to patch immediately. To balance this, we propose: (a) define P1 security vulnerabilities by CVSS >= 9 or agreed critical list, and (b) require retrospective incident notes and SLA credit exemption for verified P1 security patches.
- Response ladder: for P1 incidents we'll commit to 15 minute acknowledge and one‑hour mitigation target (see rdw_response-ladder.docx).

If GridPay legal wants a bright‑line list of CVEs/criteria we can iterate quickly. I also added language that caps monthly credits at the proposed 25% of monthly fees and a separate remediation credit bucket for repeat incidents.

I'll be available on a short call this afternoon if you want to hash the CVSS threshold live.

—Kimberly Park
Sr. Product Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_slo_matrix.xlsx, rdw_response-ladder.docx

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@gridpay.com>, GridPay Legal <legal@gridpay.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@gridpay.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MSA / Order Form — SLA: uptime thresholds, emergency patch window, and credit triggers (proposed compromise)

Claire / Tom / GridPay Legal — forwarding our proposed compromise for SLA language. Key points in the updated draft (attached):
- Measurement: rolling 7‑day smoothing window to prevent spike-driven credits.
- De‑minimis: exclude single incidents < 5 minutes unless they are part of a repeated failure pattern within 24 hours.
- Emergency patching: Redwood retains the right to apply immediate fixes for P1 security issues (CVSS >=9 or mutually agreed list). Non‑security emergency patches will have a 2‑hour notice where practicable. Retrospective reporting required for all immediate patches.
- Financials: cumulative monthly credit cap = 25% of monthly fees; separate remediation credit for repeated incidents defined as 3 or more occurrences of same root cause within 30 days.

Please review the attached redline (redline_msa_sla.pdf v3). If GridPay legal can accept the CVSS >=9 threshold for immediate security patches and the credit cap, we will prepare the DocuSign packet and route to procurement. DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?s=ABCDEF1234567890

Next steps: (1) GridPay legal signoff or counter by EOD tomorrow, (2) DocuSign sent, (3) target execution by Friday.

Thanks — appreciate the collaboration.
Rafael Mendes
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline_msa_sla.pdf (v3)
